problem:
Determine all real eigenvalues $\lambda $ of the matrix 
$O=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,O-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
O-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is given by $det(O-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st row, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(O-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & -\lambda \end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & -1-\lambda  \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}+1)+(\lambda +1) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}+\lambda +2 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}+2{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to solve this equation. We find the first root by testing some values. According to the rational zeros theorem, a list of good first guesses consists of all divisors of $2:$ 

$$
\pm 1,\pm 2
$$

Let's pick $x=1.$ Substituting to the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(1)^{3}+2(1)^{2}-(1)-2 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $\lambda =1$ is a root of the equation. So, we can factor $(\lambda -1)$ out of ${\lambda }^{3}+2{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -2$ using synthetic division:

| $1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $-1$ | $-2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | $↓$ | $1$ | $3$ | $2$ |
|  | $1$ | $3$ | $2$ | $0$ |

So, we obtain the following factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\lambda -1)({\lambda }^{2}+3\lambda +2) & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)(\lambda +2)(\lambda +1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=1,$ $\,{\lambda }_{2}=-2,\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}=-1.$
